# Model cards

Each model Najma uses has a card in `backend/ml/model_cards/` with what it does, its data, its limits and what it must not be used for.

| Model | What it does |
|---|---|
| [Best Next Game (bandit)](../../backend/ml/model_cards/best_next_game.md) | Gives `plan_next` a `bandit_gain` for each skill (weight 0.10, shown in every decision's breakdown) and picks, within the chosen skill, the game with the best Thompson sample: the game expected to move this person's estimate the most per round, with room to try games we know little about. |
| [Engagement Risk](../../backend/ml/model_cards/engagement_risk.md) | The chance that a person has no activity at all in the next 7 days, as a range (inductive Venn-Abers). Najma uses it to offer a shorter, easier session to someone who is drifting away. It is never shown as a score of the person. |
| [Fatigue Point](../../backend/ml/model_cards/fatigue_point.md) | Minutes into a session when this person's answers usually start to slow down, as a median with its middle half (25th to 75th percentile). The `monitor` node ends a session past the median and says the range: "Your answers usually start to slow down 9 to 14 minutes into a session." |
| [Growth Forecast](../../backend/ml/model_cards/growth_forecast.md) | From a person's first sessions with a kind of game, it predicts their score after k more sessions (k = 1 to 20) as an **80% range**. Najma shows it on progress curves and in coaching, always with the range (AGENTS.md rule 5). |
